notes: Two mechanisms. S->N fails by design, as in every earlier round: upstream's tests call the Flask service the agent left on port 5000, and a copy has no running process ("Connection refused"; test_flask_api_running, test_sentiment_endpoint and test_api_error_handling fail, test_model_downloaded passes). The conversion asks for /app/start.sh and starts it, so S passes. On the native side the earlier explanation (the native agent wrote no start.sh, so N->S fails) still holds: its /app has app.py and service.log but no start.sh. But this round N->S and N->s->N failed earlier, for a new reason in the measurement tool. The native agent pip-installed PyTorch into /usr/local, so the tool's restore has to unpack 5.7 GB (root-1.tar) into /usr/local, under the task's 2 GiB memory limit. The restore was killed for memory after 75.9 s (agent ending `memory_killed`), leaving /usr/local half restored. The model-loads check runs /usr/local/bin/python3, so it fails with "adapter exited with status 1" (failed/case_error). The candidate captured from that broken container records 561 removals, including 38 standard-library modules such as /usr/local/lib/python3.13/types.py, so in N->s->N the native verifier's pip fails with "ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'types'" and then "pytest: command not found". Both native cross-grades therefore say nothing about either grader. The scope difference (N passed, N->s->N failed) would have been the by-design running-service case, but here it is this broken restore.
